notEncoded.claim: MUTATION: replace the read-back `validateDataFile(reparsed, file.path)` in `modeUpdateExpected` with an empty problem list → a rewrite that does not validate is written anyway.
notEncoded.why: No input reaches it. Only a MISMATCH is rewritten and a MISMATCH always carries a non-empty observed set, so the one rule `validateDataFile` would catch cannot fire; and `scanStringArrayEnd` refuses every array it cannot splice cleanly, so the `JSON.parse` cannot fail either. The read-back is defence in depth against a future splice bug, not a branch any present input takes. Encoding it would report SURVIVED and read as coverage.

notEncoded.claim: MUTATION: make parseTap throw whenever `failed` is empty → SURVIVED becomes an exit-2 harness fault and is never reported.
notEncoded.why: The break is the ADDITION of a throw, not the removal or alteration of existing text, so there is no unique `find` anchor for it. The find/replace schema expresses deletions and substitutions of code that is present; an insertion at an arbitrary point is not addressable without an anchor that says nothing about the mechanism.

notEncoded.claim: MUTATION: replace the CAUGHT branch's condition with `false` → nothing is ever caught.
notEncoded.why: Encodable, but it is strictly dominated by `superset-is-caught` and `subset-is-caught`, which mutate the same condition in the two directions that can actually ship. A blanket `false` reddens most of the compareResult block and would pin nothing the other two do not.

notEncoded.claim: MUTATION: make validateDataFile always push a problem → every data file is rejected and the harness exits 2 without running anything, while reporting a data-file fault.
notEncoded.why: The break is the ADDITION of an unconditional push at the function entry — not the removal or alteration of any existing text. Any substitution that achieves 'always push' (e.g. seeding the problems array) reddens 'accepts a well-formed data file', 'accepts an empty replacement as a deletion', and the relative-path half of 'rejects a target outside the worktree' simultaneously, producing a superset that pins nothing the individual field-rejection tests do not already cover.

notEncoded.claim: the rmSync fallback in runMutation's finally removes a temp dir that `git worktree add` failed to register, which `worktree remove` refuses and `prune` does not touch
notEncoded.why: NOT PINNED and not cheaply pinnable, established by looking rather than assuming — the same claim was wrong twice on this branch. The `git` helper is an unexported module-level closure, so there is no injection point; and the spawn route cannot reach it, because the fault fixture throws from `assertSingleOccurrence`, which runs AFTER `worktree add` has already succeeded. Forcing `worktree add` to fail needs an engineered condition (no HEAD, a path collision, a full disk) that is neither cheap nor reliable. Recorded here because it carries no MUTATION: comment, so `--coverage` cannot report it as a gap at all — a silent hole is exactly what this list exists for. The bound on the damage is what makes leaving it acceptable: deleting the line leaks one temp dir per faulted mutation under tmpdir(), and can never produce a wrong verdict or a wrong exit code.
